item.title: Trump demands probe into ‘fake’ US GDP figures
item.description: President Donald Trump called Thursday for an investigation into a routine revision of economic growth figures as he pushed his groundless claims of interference in the US midterm elections. Trump lashed out at what he called “FAKE” figures a day after the US Commerce Department strongly revised GDP growth in the third quarter up to 4.3 percent from the previous estimate of 3.4 percent. Such updates are commonplace. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error.” Trump followed up in a lengthy second post for the US Thanksgiving holiday in which he also took aim at a series of perceived enemies and critics of his extensive makeover of the White House. “I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late,” wrote Trump. He added that it was a “RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated.” Trump’s allegation of deliberate action echoes his other recent baseless claims calling into doubt his Republican Party’s brutal defeat in the November 3 midterm elections. Democrats won control of Congress as voters hammered Trump’s Republicans over economic headwinds sparked by the Iran war and the president’s chaotic tariff policies. Throughout his two presidencies, the 80-year-old Trump has repeatedly attacked the political, legal and economic norms that have long underpinned US democracy. Trump has previously defended his economic performance by pointing to data like GDP growth, which has been robust despite the headwinds, mainly on the back of the AI boom. Issuing its new GDP estimate on Wednesday, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis said the growth “primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports.” Vanguard News The post Trump demands probe into ‘fake’ US GDP figures appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG hails Davido, Asake, others over 2027 Grammy nominations
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Federal Government has congratulated Nigerian music stars Davido, Tems, Asake, Ayra Starr, Wizkid and Burna Boy following their nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, congratulated the artistes in a post on her official X account on Thursday, describing their nominations as a source of pride for the country. Musawa noted that Nigerian artistes accounted for three of the five nominees in the Best Global Music Album category and featured in four of the five entries for Best African Music Performance. “Your music travels because it is yours. Every record also employs producers, engineers, dancers and crews, and protecting what creators own is at the heart of our work,” she wrote. She added that the country would be cheering the Nigerian nominees at the awards ceremony scheduled for February 7, 2027. The Recording Academy announced the nominees on November 16, with the six Nigerian artistes earning recognition across five categories. In the Best African Music Performance category, Asake received a nomination for his song ‘Gratitude’, while his collaboration with Wizkid, ‘Jogodo’, also made the list. Tems was nominated for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr earned a nod alongside Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’. Davido, Ayra Starr and Tems also secured nominations in the Best Global Music Album category for their respective projects, ‘Oriadé’, ‘Starrgirl’ and ‘Love Is a Kingdom’. Burna Boy earned a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira. Tems further received nominations in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories for her song ‘What You Need’. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled to hold at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States, on February 7, 2027. item.title: 2027 election: Tinubu is beatable — Baba-Ahmed
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye National Chairman of the People’s Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has described President Bola Tinubu as the most beatable president, predicting that he would lose many states in 2027 if the election is free and fair. Baba-Ahmed spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today, saying Tinubu was surrounded by people who he believed were misinforming him about his chances. “I don’t think there’s any president more beatable than Bola Tinubu. You just mentioned the fact that he is surrounded by people who are either misadvising him or misinforming him. It’s the same thing that is happening. They are telling him, ‘Oh, Mr President, you’ve already won this election.’” He alleged that APC rallies did not reflect genuine support, claiming attendees were paid to attend. “How did you see the people at the rally? In APC rallies, there is ‘Bamayi, Bamayi.’ They bring people in, they fill their pockets with money, and they take them to stay there,” he said. Asked whether Tinubu would lose the election, Baba-Ahmed replied: “Yes. If the election is free and fair, he will lose many states.” He said he hoped the election would be credible, urging the Independent National Electoral Commission to provide a level playing field and the judiciary to handle election disputes fairly. “I’m hoping it will be, for the sake of the country, for the future of our children, and for the future of everything. And honestly, I’m hoping that INEC somewhere along the line will find the will and the ability to provide a level playing field, not to rig this election, and I’m hoping the judiciary, which traditionally sorts out anywhere between 60 and 70 per cent of the elections, will be fair,” he said. Baba-Ahmed also criticised what he described as the ruling party’s distribution of money and vehicles to people facing hardship, questioning why such resources were not used to address insecurity, infrastructure and the cost of living. The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. She urged journalists to go beyond reporting statistics and highlight the experiences of vulnerable children and families. “Statistics only matter when they move us to protect the child behind the number. We need the media to humanize the numbers, keep children in the headlines year-round and spotlight the solutions that are working across Nigeria,” she said. Dr. Sanwo-Olu In her keynote address, Lagos State First Lady, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, said supporting mothers and investing early in children were essential to building a healthier and better-educated generation. She said the Babajide Sanwo-Olu administration remained committed to inclusive child development and gender-responsive governance, ensuring that every child, irrespective of gender, had the opportunity to realise his or her potential. On the proposed review of the Lagos State Child’s Rights Law 2015, she said: “As we undertake the review of the Child’s Rights Law 2015, we have before us a unique opportunity to strengthen our legal and institutional framework in ways that respond to emerging realities while safeguarding the best interests of every child.” Providing further insight into the child health situation, Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Primary Health Care Board, Dr Ibrahim Akinwunmi-Mustafa, said Nigeria had made progress in reducing under-five mortality but continued to face serious challenges in newborn survival and childhood malnutrition. “Under-five deaths have fallen from 132 to 110 per 1,000 live births since 2018. But newborn deaths have barely moved, and four in ten Nigerian children are still stunted.” He disclosed that child stunting in Lagos was about 17 per cent, compared with 40 per cent nationally, while an estimated 120,000 to 130,000 children in the state had never received a single vaccine. “Most of them live in our informal settlements, riverine communities and fast-growing areas,” he said. Mustafa called for stronger primary healthcare financing, investment in frontline health workers and improved access to antenatal care, nutrition counselling, immunisation and birth registration. He also urged journalists to support public health campaigns, counter misinformation and hold government and other stakeholders accountable. “To our friends in the media: you are partners in this work, not spectators,” he said. Airtel Also speaking, the Director of Corporate Communications and Corporate Social Responsibility at Airtel Nigeria, Adefemi Adeniran, said a child’s background, economic circumstances or developmental differences should not determine his or her future. “Neither the economic circumstances of a child’s parent, background nor their developmental differences should determine a child’s prospects in life. Keeping them alive is our fundamental obligation. Enabling them to learn is our collective responsibility. Creating conditions for them to thrive must be our shared ambition,” he said. Also the DAME Trustee, Mr. Lanre Idowu, said the partnership between UNICEF, NGE and DAME was helping to strengthen child-rights journalism through training, access to credible evidence, field visits and recognition of excellent reporting. On his part, UNICEF Nigeria Goodwill Ambassador and musician, Cobhams Asuquo, highlighted the role of music in communicating messages about child survival and development. “Music is a powerful tool. It can take an important message beyond the statistics and help people connect with the real lives and experiences behind it. With the First 1,000 Days of Life song, we wanted families and communities to understand that what we do for a child from the very beginning, the nutrition, care and support we provide, can shape that child’s future,” he said. Children also participated in the discussions, questioning decision-makers on how they would ensure that poverty, gender, disability and family circumstances did not deny any child access to healthcare, education and protection. Their performances, including “The First 1,000 Days of Life” and “I Am a Nigerian Child,” reinforced the importance of including children’s voices in decisions affecting their future. The symposium coincided with UNICEF’s 80th anniversary, with participants renewing calls for sustained government leadership, adequate financing, private sector investment, community participation and media accountability to secure a better future for Nigerian children. item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, justice for survivors
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have renewed calls for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a special reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s landmark publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said although the achievement deserved celebration, sexual violence remained a difficult issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. item.title: ‘We wished you stayed longer’ – Nkem Owoh mourns Pete Edochie
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Nkem Owoh has paid tribute to his late colleague and friend, Pete Edochie, expressing regret that the legendary actor did not live long enough to celebrate his 80th birthday. Owoh, in a tribute shared on his Instagram page, described Edochie as a dear brother and friend who made people believe in humanity through the way he lived and treated those around him. The actor recalled that Edochie had celebrated his 70th birthday in a special way, during which he spoke about their shared experience in the movie Ikuku . Owoh said he had looked forward to sharing his own story about Edochie when the latter turned 80 on March 7, 2027. However, he lamented that death had taken his friend before the milestone birthday. “I was waiting to tell my own story about you on your 80th birthday, which is on 7th March, 2027. But death had another plan. Who are we to question God?” he wrote. The actor added that he and others had wished Edochie could live a little longer to witness the celebration they had anticipated. “We would have wished you stayed a bit longer to see that great day we were all looking forward to,” he said. Describing the late actor with his traditional titles, including Ogadagidi, Ebubedike and Ononenyi na Nteje, Owoh said Edochie had lived a fulfilled life and prayed for blessings upon his family. “You lived well and we are assured of your place in heaven. Rest well, my friend and brother. May your passing bring immeasurable blessings to your family,” he wrote. He concluded his tribute by describing Edochie as an irreplaceable legend and bidding him farewell with the words, “Ijeoma, Ebube Dike Ndi Igbo.” The post ‘We wished you stayed longer’ – Nkem Owoh mourns Pete Edochie appeared first on Vanguard News .

Bianca also expressed disappointment with some Igbo political elites who, despite benefiting from the influence and political legacy of her late husband, had abandoned him and failed to sustain the ideals he stood for. She said Ojukwu’s legacy should not be reduced to the celebration of his military exploits, titles, speeches and political struggles, but should be understood through his convictions, humanity and commitment to justice and dignity. The minister said her late husband was a soldier, statesman, intellectual and patriarch whose life was driven by a profound belief in justice and the right of people to live without fear. Reflecting on the painful history of the Igbo, particularly the 1966 pogroms, displacement and civil war, she said remembrance of Ojukwu should serve as a commitment to preventing a recurrence of such tragedies rather than merely celebrating the circumstances that made him famous. She called on traditional rulers to provide moral direction, political leaders to rise above personal interests, businessmen and women to invest in the homeland, and young people to channel their energies into innovation rather than destruction. Bianca also urged Igbo youths in the diaspora to resist the lure of illicit wealth, warning that the pursuit of criminal proceeds had brought disgrace and left some languishing in detention instead of building meaningful futures. She urged them to become ambassadors of their people and contribute to rebuilding a homeland where investors could operate confidently, businesses could thrive and families could celebrate Christmas, weddings and other festivities without fear. The minister lamented the deteriorating security and economic environment in parts of the South-East, saying the region could not attract investment or encourage its children to return home if communities remained frightened, businesses abandoned and streets empty. “Our land must once again become a place where our children are excited to return,” she said, adding that investors must feel confident to establish businesses in the region. She stressed that Ojukwu’s legacy could only endure if his values became visible in the lives of those who inherited it, noting that annual memorials alone were insufficient to sustain the memory of a great leader. Taking a swipe at successive leaders over the failure to properly immortalise prominent Igbo figures, Bianca cited the prolonged delay in completing the Zik Mausoleum, lamenting what she described as a troubling lack of commitment to preserving the legacies of leaders who made enormous contributions to the people. Bianca regretted that it took the former President Muhammadu Buhari to build a mausoleum where Zik was buried 22 years after his death, while successive administrations in Anambra looked away. She said some leaders lived as though they would never die, but were eventually forgotten, unlike a few whose courage and contributions continued to inspire generations. Bianca thanked those who had sustained Ojukwu’s memory through the annual memorial, saying such acts ensured that his story, valour and ideals would continue to be told to generations yet unborn. She particularly poured encomiums on BIM MASSOB Leader, Chief Ralph Uwazurike, for honouring her husband by instituting the annual memorial series. Uwazurike demands Nnamdi Kanu’s release Says Igbo need new leader, faults political elite Chief Uwazurike, in his speech, renewed his call for the release of Kanu, insisting that he committed no offence warranting his continued detention. He argued that Kanu deserved freedom, drawing a comparison with Yoruba agitator, Sunday Igboho, who he said had been released. He said the only difference between Kanu and Igboho was that the latter had a brother who was Nigeria’s President. “Where is Sunday Igboho? Kanu didn’t commit any offence that is bigger or more sinister than that of Igboho. The only difference is that Sunday Igboho has a brother who is presently the President of Nigeria,” Uwazurike said. He added that Kanu would have been released if Peter Obi were Nigeria’s President. Uwazurike, who advocated non-violent agitation for Biafra, cautioned youths against resorting to violence, saying they had misunderstood the concept of self-determination and allowed social media to distort the struggle. He argued that violence was inconsistent with the principles of self-determination, urging the younger generation to embrace peaceful advocacy. “I urge the new generation of indigenous people to abide by the principles of non-violence,” he said, citing Mahatma Gandhi, whom he described as his idol. The MASSOB founder said he had no regrets over the sacrifices he made in the course of the Biafra struggle, including persecution and the burning of his residence by state actors, insisting he was prepared to make even greater sacrifices if Biafra could be achieved through peaceful means. “I want to even sacrifice more if Biafra could be actualised through non-violence,” he said, warning that resorting to force would undermine the struggle. Uwazurike also lamented the absence of a unifying Igbo leader following Ojukwu’s death, expressing hope that another leader would emerge whom the people could rally behind. He said Ojukwu remained the leader many Igbo still identified with despite his death, adding that the annual memorial was an avenue to promote unity among Igbo people. Uwazurike dismissed the absence of political elites at the memorial, saying the event was about the people rather than the political class, whom he accused of being divided by personal interests. He said the unity of the Igbo remained one of Ojukwu’s major legacies and urged the people to sustain it. The ceremony, which attracted cultural displays, masquerades and match past by delegations from different states in the Old Eastern Region, also featured lectures and goodwill messages. item.title: Super Falcons: Eguavon invites 24 players for Algeria friendlies
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria’s Super Falcons have named a 24 player squad for their upcoming international friendlies against Algeria, with goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie and forward Asisat Oshoala among the key players selected. The squad, announced by interim coach Augustine Eguavoen, will face Algeria on November 30 in Algiers before meeting the North African side again on December 4 in Tizi-Ouzou. Captain Rasheedat Ajibade is, however, absent from the list as she continues her recovery from surgery. The two matches are expected to provide the Falcons with an opportunity to prepare for their Olympic qualifying encounter against Morocco scheduled for March 2027. Nnadozie, Comfort Erhabor and Christiana Uzoma are the three goalkeepers selected for the fixtures. The defensive department comprises Michelle Alozie, Shukurat Oladipo, Glory Ogbonna, Oluwatosin Demehin, Glory Edet, Valentina Uroko and Nicole Payne. In midfield, Eguavoen has called up Christy Ucheibe, Joy Igbokwe, Regina Otu, Fatimoh Solaty, Suliat Abideen, Toni Payne and Jennifer Echegini. Oshoala will lead the attacking options alongside Folashade Ijamilusi, Shakirat Moshood, Blessing Okpe, Joy Omewa, Blessing Nkor and Olamide Adugbe. The friendlies form part of Nigeria’s preparations as the team looks to secure qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games. item.title: NDC using ‘rig and die’ slogan to mobilise for mass rigging – Keyamo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo SAN, has accused the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC of using the “rig and die” slogan as a cover to mobilise its members and “rig the elections massively.” Keyamo made the claim on Thursday in a post on his X account. He was reacting to a clarification of the slogan by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. “There is no need for Peter Obi to clarify the ‘rig and die’ slogan and do damage control. We know what it means. The slogan is nothing but a subterfuge for them to mobilise themselves and rig the elections massively as they did in a part of the country in 2023 but still failed”, he said. The minister asked what would stop a party that is “sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents” from rigging elections itself. “If a party in a contest with other parties is sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents, what stops that same party from rigging the elections itself? Are they saints?” he asked. He argued that no party can be both contestant and referee. “You cannot be a participant in a contest, yet you want to act as the umpire under the guise that you don’t trust the umpire! That is creating a graver absurdity than the one you’re trying to solve!” he said. The slogan became a national talking point after a former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District, used it at a campaign event in Uvwie, Delta State, in October. “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him!” Omo-Agege said, adding: “It is rig and die.” Tension over the slogan grew after gunmen attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign team at Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, this Monday. His media adviser, Sunny Areh, said four people were killed and four others critically injured, while Omo-Agege was unhurt. Other reports put the death toll at six. Keyamo condemned the killings the same day. He asked promoters of the slogan to “publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature.” “It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he said then. Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, later visited the families of the victims. Obi also spoke to Channels Television on the slogan. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die,'” he said. Obi was also reported to have said that the slogan “simply means, do not rig the election. We want a free and fair election. It never meant campaign and die.” He also defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement, who carry sticks to political gatherings. He said they have never used them to harm anyone. However, Keyamo dismissed the explanation, saying Obi’s camp was the one casting itself as the aggrieved party. “This is a classic case of the villain playing the victim,” he said. item.title: Aubameyang escapes injury in car crash ahead of Barcelona clash
item.description: Deportivo La Coruña striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang escaped unhurt after his car was involved in a collision with another vehicle while he was driving to the club’s training ground on Thursday. The incident occurred at about 9:23am on the AP-9 motorway in the Piadela area, near the junction with the A6, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Both vehicles sustained damage, but nobody involved in the accident was injured. Aubameyang continued his journey to Deportivo’s Abegondo training base after the collision and joined his teammates for the scheduled group session. The Gabon international later played down the incident, describing it as a minor scare and expressing relief that everyone involved was safe. “It was just a little scare. These things happen in life. The most important thing is that the other person involved in the accident is fine, and so am I,” he said. The incident comes as Deportivo prepare to host Barcelona at the Riazor Stadium next Sunday, a fixture that will see Aubameyang face his former club. The striker had recently returned to action after recovering from a knee injury that kept him out for a period. He resumed playing at the beginning of November, gradually increasing his involvement in the team. He also experienced ankle discomfort during training last week and underwent medical examinations before recovering sufficiently to travel with the squad for their match against Alavés in Vitoria. Aubameyang had made an impressive start to the season, scoring five goals in his first five official appearances before the knee injury interrupted his run. His availability will be important to Deportivo as they prepare for the Barcelona encounter, with the club relying on his experience and attacking contribution. item.title: Navy dismantles four illegal refineries, recovers 112,525 litres in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has dismantled four illegal refining sites and uncovered approximately 112,525 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in separate operations in Rivers State. The Director of Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this on Thursday, saying the operations exposed repeated attempts by oil thieves to reactivate previously dismantled illegal refining sites. He said the operations were conducted on November 25, 2026, by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh and Forward Operating Base (FOB) Bonny in Ogbogolo Community, Ahoada West Local Government Area, and George Pepple Community, Bonny Local Government Area. According to him, personnel of NNS Soroh discovered two illegal refining sites at Ogbogolo, containing approximately 15,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and 525 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. The sites also contained three cooking drum ovens, two dugout pits and other equipment used for illegal refining activities. In a separate operation at George Pepple Community, Folorunsho said personnel of FOB Bonny discovered two illegal refining sites comprising 13 dugout pits. He said seven of the pits contained approximately 97,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil, while four contained water and two were freshly excavated. Folorunsho said all identified facilities and recovered petroleum products were handled in accordance with established procedures. He noted that the operations exposed continued attempts by oil thieves to relocate and reactivate illegal refining activities following previous military operations. “By targeting the facilities used for processing and storing stolen petroleum products, the Nigerian Navy is constraining the operational capacity of criminal operators and disrupting activities that undermine the country’s oil and gas industry,” he said. The Navy spokesman reiterated the service’s commitment to sustaining operations against crude oil theft, illegal bunkering and related criminal activities, particularly to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure. He added that the operations were aimed at safeguarding Nigeria’s energy resources and national economic interests. item.title: Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has reiterated his administration’s decision not to negotiate with bandits terrorising the state, insisting that efforts would instead focus on reclaiming ungoverned areas and restoring security. Lawal stated this on Thursday at the graduation ceremony of the Zamfara Forest Guards held at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, Gusau. More than 1,000 forest guards graduated after undergoing training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement and the rule of law. The armed forest guard initiative was launched by President Bola Tinubu on May 24, 2025, to train residents to secure forests and other ungoverned areas across the country. At the ceremony, Lawal expressed appreciation to Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the initiative. He also commended security agencies, the training coordinator and instructors for their roles in preparing the guards for service. Addressing the graduates and their families, the governor said Zamfara needed to reclaim its vast ungoverned areas, which he said had become hideouts for bandits and other criminal groups. “We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists. “This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services. “Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods,” he said. The governor said his administration had invested substantially in security agencies over the past three years through the provision of operational equipment, vehicles, surveillance technology and logistical support. He listed the equipment provided to security agencies as more than 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 operational pick-up vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles and over 1,000 specialised motorcycles. He added that additional vehicles and motorcycles had also been supplied to the Homegrown Community Protection Guards. On surveillance, Lawal said the state had acquired drones, including an 80-metre endurance model capable of covering up to 50 kilometres and operating continuously for eight hours. According to him, the equipment would improve reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain. item.title: Fofana apologises over unauthorised interview; Alonso says issue is closed
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says Wesley Fofana has apologised for giving an unauthorised interview in which he laughed about the penalty miss that knocked the club out of the Carabao Cup against Liverpool. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Friday’s Premier League game against Nottingham Forest, Alonso said the matter had been addressed and Fofana would be available to play. “We have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it wasn’t the right moment. The content wasn’t right,” Alonso said. “We are here to take things seriously and he said it wouldn’t be repeated. We know it’s something we don’t want and they are not going to be repeated.” In the interview with French YouTuber Zack Nani, Fofana said he could “laugh about” the penalty miss. The defender also spoke about having considered retiring from football during one of his spells out with injury at Chelsea. Alonso also urged his players to respond to their 4-1 defeat by Leeds, saying they had failed to meet the standards required to compete. “On Saturday, we missed not just players but many basics to compete in the game. That’s been clear during the week,” he said. “We talked about having those basics to compete, to know what it takes to be ready for each game and we will need that tomorrow.” He said the defeat had been analysed but should not be forgotten. “The idea is that we don’t forget. In the future, we’ll say those standards are not acceptable at this level.” The post Fofana apologises over unauthorised interview; Alonso says issue is closed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will on Saturday conduct a mock test of its voter accreditation technology in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise will take place in 406 polling units across the state’s 18 local government areas between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. INEC said the exercise was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify potential technical challenges ahead of the general elections. In a statement, the Deputy Director and Head of Department, Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, said two polling units had been selected from each of the 203 registration areas in the state. The Commission explained that the test would assess how the BVAS performs under different conditions and enable it to address any technical issues identified before the elections. INEC stressed that the exercise was not an election, adding that no voter would cast a ballot for any candidate or political party. It urged residents of the affected polling units, community leaders, political parties, civil society organisations and journalists to cooperate with its officials to ensure a successful exercise. The Commission also cautioned against the spread of rumours and fake news, urging residents to obtain election-related information only through its official communication channels. It said the mock accreditation exercise was part of its early preparations to ensure the smooth deployment of technology and the conduct of credible elections in 2027. I think the President has done a good job.” ‎‎Both former leaders spoke on Thursday when a presidential delegation, led by the Chief of Staff to the President, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, visited them at their residences in Minna, the Niger State capital. ‎‎Speaking to journalists after a closed-door meeting with Babangida, Gbajabiamila stated that the former Military President was impressed with Tinubu’s work and had reaffirmed his support for the President. ‎‎He said both Babangida and Abubakar had been supportive of the Tinubu administration, describing them as major figures in Nigeria’s history. ‎‎“These are two personalities that you cannot write the history of Nigeria without them occupying very major chapters in that history book,” Gbajabiamila said. ‎‎“He is very happy with what Mr President is doing. He is very happy with his work, and he continues to support him and wishes him all the very best and the best of luck in the forthcoming elections,” he added. ‎‎Abubakar, speaking on behalf of the National Peace Committee, urged Nigerians to prioritise peace ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎‎“I want to pray for Nigeria so that we can have a peaceful election, because I keep saying, on behalf of the National Peace Committee, that we need peace in the country,” he said. ‎‎“Without peace, there will be no country, and if there is no country, there wouldn’t be an election. So, I am praying to our people that they should please give peace a chance so that we can have a peaceful election,” Abubakar added. We we visited them – Gbajabiamila ‎‎Gbajabiamila said Tinubu directed the visit after returning from Borno State on Wednesday, to ascertain the well-being of the former leaders and report back to him. ‎‎He said the President had wanted to maintain regular communication with the former leaders but had been constrained by official engagements, including campaign trips across the country. ‎‎Gbajabiamila also said Tinubu asked him to discuss other matters privately during the visit, but did not disclose the details. ‎‎The former Speaker of the House of Representatives said Abubakar thanked Tinubu for maintaining contact with the former leaders despite his campaign activities and the demands of governance. ‎‎“I want to thank him for this simple act of remembering us, despite the period of campaigning. He still remembers us, that we are still here in Minna,” he said. ‎He also appreciated the President for the support extended to him during his medical trip abroad. ‎‎“I want, through you, to thank Mr President for the support he has always shown to us, especially when I was going for my medicals. He sent me some support. I want to thank him for that,” Abubakar said. ‎‎He added that Tinubu had also asked Vice President Kashim Shettima to check on him during the BRICS meeting in India. ‎‎Abubakar said his health had improved considerably and that Babangida was also doing well. ‎‎“We are doing well, as you have observed. We are doing very well, and my health is improving greatly. My brother across the hill is also doing fine,” he said. Delegation ‎‎The delegation included the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris; Special Adviser to the President on Policy and Coordination, Hadiza Bala-Usman; former Minister of State for Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Yusuf Tanko Sununu; and former Minister of Transportation, Sa’idu Ahmed Alkali. ‎‎Others were Deputy Governor of Niger State, Yakubu Garba; member representing Kuru/Bebeji Federal Constituency, Hon. Abdulmumini Jibrin Kofa; member representing Surulere I Federal Constituency, Hon. Fuad Kayode Laguda; Special Adviser to the President on National Assembly Matters (House of Representatives), Dr Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart; and Director-General and Chief Negotiator of the Nigerian Office for Trade Negotiations (NOTN), Hon. Photo: Taiwo Adesina/Channels TV He said the three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025 attracted more than 11 million registrations, with over 10.77 million new registrants retained. The commission also received approximately 311,000 complaints during the claims-and-objections exercise, of which about 232,000 were found to be genuine and addressed. “By the time we are putting the verified and cleaned-up register together, the national voters’ register is reduced from 103 million to 100 million,” Amupitan said. Peter Obi, who was of the Labour Party, finished third with 6,101,533 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso, then of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), secured 1,496,687 votes. item.title: Gov Okpebholo Denies Involvement In Attack On NDC Members, Obi’s Supporters
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has denied allegations linking him, the All Progressives Congress (APC), or its supporters to the alleged violent attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during the party’s activities in Benin City, the state capital. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Ehor, headquarters of Uhunmwonde Local Government Area, and Ekpoma in Esan West, the governor described the allegations as unfounded, insisting that neither the state government nor the APC had any reason to disrupt opposition political activities. ﻿ Okpebholo alleged that the incident involved irresponsible elements who were fighting among themselves, dismissing claims of government involvement. He said his priority remained the development of Edo State, stressing that he would not divert his attention to political violence or activities capable of undermining the progress of the state. The governor recalled that he did not engage thugs during his senatorial and governorship campaigns, alleging that a police officer was killed during the governorship election by individuals he claimed were linked to the opposition. He also vowed to sustain his administration’s crackdown on cultism and other criminal activities, insisting that elections should be conducted based on the principle of one man, one vote. Okpebholo urged residents to participate actively in the electoral process, while thanking APC supporters for their turnout at the rally. Earlier, Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa urged the people to vote for APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections, while party chairman Jarrett Tenebe commended the governor’s efforts in tackling kidnapping and cultism, urging continued support for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. Political thugs on Wednesday attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the NDC in Benin City, after the party said it received an intelligence report on a possible attack at its town hall meeting in Benin, where its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, was expected to address supporters. The Edo State Coordinator of the party’s campaign council, John Yakubu, said the party had been informed of plans to disrupt the event, as members prepared to leave their campaign office to receive Obi at the airport. Videos obtained by our correspondent showed blood stains on the party convoys, including bullet casings seen on the floor of the party’s campaign office. The incident came barely 48 hours after former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy was also attacked during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, in Delta State on Monday. Last week, the Edo State Police Command commenced an investigation into an attack on the NDC secretariat in Afuze, Owan East Local Government Area, by armed men alleged to be members of the Edo State Security Network. item.title: 2027: Don’t Vote for Me If You Won’t Vote Tinubu, Nwifuru Tells Ebonyi Residents
item.description: The ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has officially flagged off its 2027 governorship and general election campaigns in Afikpo Local Government Area, with Governor Francis Nwifuru declaring that the party’s campaign is an all-encompassing mission aimed at securing victory for all APC flagbearers, beginning with President Bola Tinubu. ﻿ Leading the charge, Governor Nwifuru, accompanied by his deputy, Princess Patricia Obila, arrived in Afikpo to a rousing welcome from party stalwarts, stakeholders, and thousands of enthusiastic supporters ahead of the grand rally. “We are here to campaign for our party, and our party is very comprehensive,” he said while addressing the massive crowd. “We are here to campaign for all our candidates, starting with President Bola Tinubu. On the first day of the election, you will be voting for President Bola Tinubu. “Vote the broom, the symbol of unity. On that same day, vote for Senator Anthony Ani, and for the great people of Afikpo/Edda Federal Constituency, vote for Joseph Ekumankama.” In a striking display of loyalty, the governor urged Ebonyi electorate to prioritise President Tinubu’s re-election above his own second-term bid, warning that an opposition victory at the federal level would stall ongoing critical infrastructure projects in the state. “If anyone will not vote for the President, that person should not vote for me,” Nwifuru stated firmly, stressing that he would not have the moral standing to face the President if Ebonyi failed to deliver. “Voting for me is not as important as voting for the President. If the President does not win, the opposition will not complete the ongoing projects; they won’t continue them; they will abandon them,” he said. Reiterating the state’s commitment to delivering 1.3 million votes for President Tinubu, Nwifuru urged residents to resist political deception, noting that the President had rewarded Ebonyi generously despite the state giving him only 14 percent of its votes in 2023. “I am not disturbed because I know the President means well for us,” he stated. “No President has ever started and finished a major project in Ebonyi, but Tinubu has done it for us.” “He appointed our own son as the Minister of Works, giving us the biggest ministry. This time around, we owe the President. We are indebted to him for the projects in Ebonyi. Take this message home: no other person will love us the way Tinubu loves us. It is payback time.” The governor pointed to the ongoing Calabar–Abuja Superhighway (Coastal Road corridor) passing through the state and the construction of a new cement factory as tangible proof of federal backing. “The road to Afikpo is evidence of what the President has done for us. The President is not just constructing roads; he is the brain behind our new cement factory. “That factory is under construction because of him, and he has provided the funds for us to build it. Building industries will lift a lot of our people out of poverty,” the governor said.

item.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
item.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people. The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away.The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability.The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded.More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Flames And Smoke In 2018, the government issued a decision banning heavy transport vehicles from accessing the ring road around Greater Cairo from 6:00 am to midnight. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars.Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared.”We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster.”Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars.Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared.”We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster.”Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded.
